question: In the measurements list, what should each measurement be called?
context: The mock shows friendly names like Save Changes / width. A screenshot is just pixels, so friendly names have to come from somewhere: you, the app reading the text in the image, or nowhere.

options.label: Simple automatic names you can rename
options.summary: Each row names itself from what it measures, like Width 128 px or Gap 16 px, and you can double-click any row to rename it.
pros: Renaming the few rows that matter takes seconds
cons: A long list of Width and Gap rows looks samey until you rename
options.mitigation: Rows also show a small thumbnail of where they point, so samey names still find their element.

options.label: Read names from the screenshot text
options.summary: The app reads nearby text in the image, so a measurement of a button labeled Save Changes calls itself Save Changes / width, like the mock.
pros: The list reads like a real spec with no effort
cons: Text reading can be wrong or slow, and misnamed rows are worse than plain ones
options.mitigation: Fall back to the simple name whenever the text read is not confident, and keep rename available.

options.label: No names, just values
options.summary: Rows show only the kind and number, like width 128 px. Nothing to name, nothing to rename.
pros: The least to build and the least to explain
cons: Twenty rows of bare numbers are hard to scan, and the exported list reads poorly
options.mitigation: None really; this trades readability away.
